assessment.text: The premise holds on this record: the newest 8-K reports the Board accepted Huang's resignation as President, CEO and director, effective immediately, superseding the 10-K that still lists him.

The claim's weight rests on the step from that fact to a buy decision, and nothing in the record backs that step: the filing names an interim CEO who keeps the CFO role and an open search, which describes unsettled leadership rather than an improvement.

Every operating figure in the record predates the departure, so the strong results are evidence about the business under Huang, not about it without him; revenue growth sped up to +105.9% and operating margin reached its 8-quarter high of 66.2% while he led.
The two corollaries came out as the claim implies only because they test the pre-departure quarter; they cannot show anything the resignation caused.

The valuation was struck at a 2026-09-30 price, before the resignation, and already needed 13.4% a year revenue growth for 10 years at a 65.2% margin held every year, a pace 0 of 40 comparably sized filers reached, so a buy case cannot lean on the departure having been priced in.
Net: the premise is true, the reasoning is unsupported, and the departure removes a leader under whom the record shows results the price depends on continuing.

case_for.text: The fact itself is not in dispute, and the business the new leadership inherits is still accelerating, with operating margin up 5.4 percentage points on a year earlier from gross margin, R&D and other cost leverage.
Deferred revenue grew +215.1% against revenue growth of +105.9%, so work billed ahead of delivery was building at the newest quarter and does not depend on who signs the next order.

case_against.text: Leadership turnover was broad in 2026, with the chief accounting officer and the head of worldwide field operations also leaving, so the CEO exit lands on a management bench already in transition.

The price leaves little room for a stumble: with operating margin at the industry's 90th percentile instead of the trailing level, it would need 28.1% a year, so any erosion of execution after the change weighs directly on what the price requires.
Receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1 a year before, a collection trend an interim CEO who is also CFO must now watch alongside a search.

decides.text: Whether results in quarters filed after 2026-11-11 hold the growth and margin set under Huang; the record has none yet, and the next 10-Q is the evidence that would tell.
Who the Board names as permanent CEO, which the record cannot foresee and which a later 8-K would report.
Whether the market price after the resignation differs from the 2026-09-30 price the valuation uses; the record holds no later price.

would_change.text: An 8-K naming a permanent CEO would replace the interim arrangement the challenging finding rests on.
An operating margin in the first post-departure quarter below the year-earlier 60.8% would show the departure coinciding with a reversal of the margin gain.
Quarterly revenue falling below the $96.22B of Q2 FY2027 would break the 8-quarter run of rises set under Huang.

assessment.text: The premise holds on this record: all four quarters clear 70%, the trailing-twelve-month and year-on-year corollaries come out as the claim implies, and a filing quote ties the level to Blackwell being the majority of revenue.
The cushion is thinner than the latest 75.0% suggests: the tightest quarter, Q3 FY2026, cleared the line by 3.4 percentage points, only 1.69x a typical quarterly move.

This is also a recent condition, not a settled one: the test held in only 6 of 20 past readings, and the margin was as low as 60.5% in Q1 FY2026, the quarter just before the four-quarter window opens.

The step from the claim to buying now is not backed by the record, because the price already leans on high profitability: the reverse DCF at the 2026-09-30 price assumes a 65.2% operating margin every year and still needs 13.4% annual revenue growth for 10 years.

Holding the margin is therefore what the price requires rather than an edge over it; the same calculation at the industry's 90th-percentile operating margin of 26.6% needs 28.1% a year, so any margin slippage moves the required growth sharply.
The claim is true and relevant to the decision, but on its own it confirms an assumption embedded in the valuation rather than supplying a reason to buy.

case_for.text: The margin is exceptional against its industry, ranking 4 of 63 SIC 3674 filers against a class median of 41.2%, which makes the level a structural feature of recent years rather than a one-quarter spike.
It rose 2.6 percentage points on a year earlier while revenue grew +105.9%, so the high margin was kept through rapid scale-up rather than at its expense.
Resampling the measure's own past changes, the test held through each of the next 4 quarters in 69% of paths, a description of past volatility rather than a forecast.

case_against.text: Inventory stood at 119.3 days of cost of revenue against 105.6 a year before, with the balance up +111.0% against cost of revenue up +86.8%, a build that the record cannot explain but that bears watching for margin pressure.
Against the last two years the margin is 0.2 percentage points below its peak, so the record shows a plateau, not continued expansion to drive upside.
No filer in 0 of 40 comparable ten-year spans grew as fast as the price needs, so the margin's durability is necessary but far from sufficient for the purchase case.

decides.text: Whether the margin keeps clearing 70% from a cushion of 3.4 percentage points in its weakest recent quarter, given that a 60.5% quarter sits just outside the window.
Whether the inventory build to 119.3 days resolves into sales or into charges against cost of revenue, which the record cannot yet show.
Whether operating margin stays near the 65.2% the price assumes, since the claim matters to the decision only through that assumption.

would_change.text: A quarterly gross margin below 70% in a later filing would break the four-quarter test.
A quarterly operating margin below the 65.2% the reverse DCF assumes would show the price's margin assumption failing even if gross margin holds.
Inventory rising above the $31.57B reported for Q2 FY2027 would extend the build that could precede margin pressure.

decides.text: The claim turns on whether sequential growth resumes speeding up, since year-over-year acceleration alone can come from an easy base.
It also turns on data-center revenue reported by quarter, which this record does not hold, and on whether receivables keep outgrowing revenue.

would_change.text: Quarterly revenue falling below the $96.22B of the quarter ended 2026-07-26 would show demand no longer rising sequentially, let alone accelerating.
Deferred revenue dropping below the $6.41B at 2026-07-26 would remove the sign of customers paying ahead of delivery.
Receivables rising above $63.06B while revenue stalls would point to revenue carried on credit rather than demand.

analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

weakest_why.text: c1 is the claim the decision is built on, and its premise is true. The step from that premise to buying has no backing anywhere in the record: the only post-departure facts are an interim arrangement and an open search.
Its two corollaries come out as the claim implies only because they test Q2 FY2027, a quarter run under Huang, so they cannot show anything the resignation caused.
The valuation was struck at a 2026-09-30 price, before the 2026-11-12 filing. It leans on a 65.2% operating margin held every year, which is the very record of results the departure puts in question.

strongest_for.text: Demand has been strengthening: year-on-year growth sped up from +85.2% to +105.9% and revenue rose in each of 8 quarters. Deferred revenue up +215.1% points to customers paying ahead rather than buying on credit.
Profitability is exceptional and still improving. Gross margin ranks 4 of 63 in its industry, and gross margin alone added +2.6 percentage points to the year-on-year operating margin gain.
The growth the price needs is modest beside what the company is doing. The required 13.4% a year sits far below the latest +105.9%, and the whole sensitivity grid runs only from 6.5% to 19.7%.

strongest_against.text: Earnings are not turning into cash. Over four quarters, free cash flow fell $65.87B short of net income as receivables rose $35.25B and inventory $16.61B. Conversion has fallen at every annual reading, and it ranks 32 of 38 in its industry.
Working capital is outgrowing sales. Inventory days rose to 119.3 from 105.6 and receivable days to 59.6 from 54.1, either of which could precede margin or collection pressure.

Low as it looks, the price's 13.4% a year for 10 years implies year-10 revenue 1.5 times the largest any filer reported, and 0 of 40 comparably sized filers grew that fast. The 70% gross margin line has held in only 6 of 20 past readings.

bottom_line.text: The thesis's central claim is unsupported. Huang's departure is a fact, but nothing in the record links it to a reason to buy. The 8-K describes an interim CEO who keeps the CFO role and a search still open, which is unsettled leadership rather than an improvement.

Every operating figure in the record predates the resignation. The acceleration to +105.9% revenue growth and the 8-quarter-high 66.2% operating margin therefore describe the business under Huang, not after him.

The claims that hold (margins above 70%, accelerating revenue) are what the price already requires rather than an edge over it. At the 2026-09-30 price, the reverse DCF assumes a 65.2% operating margin every year and still needs 13.4% growth a year for 10 years, a pace 0 of 40 comparably sized filers reached.

The cash claim fails, and the gap is widening. Cash conversion has fallen to 0.70x over four quarters and 0.40x in the latest quarter, so the 28.5× earnings multiple flatters the stock against a free cash flow yield of 2.3%.
The doubling claim attaches a real fact to the wrong year: fiscal 2026 grew 65.5%, after 114.2% the year before. That error weakens the thesis's reading of the record more than the decision itself.

The record cannot show results after the resignation, the permanent CEO, or any price after 2026-09-30. A careful investor would want the next 10-Q and an 8-K naming a permanent CEO before relying on the departure as a reason for anything.
